agent_vs_you: The agent recorded "Make it fun! You pick the vibe" as tone=fun and then planned only the mechanics: one assemble of the five photos in input order, 1.6 s each, with no music, no captions and no comic beat. When the user hands over the vibe, making it fun is the producer's job: an upbeat track, a joke timed to each picture, cuts on the beat. The rule it followed ("photos for a reel go straight into assemble, no image-to-video unless they ask for motion") is about not animating needlessly. It says nothing about dropping the music, and the reel template next to it includes music. Its extra "fit full photos within the vertical canvas with padding rather than cropping" is also something assemble does not do: assemble crops every picture to fill 9:16. So the 5:3 beach photo was cut to its middle third, clipping both friends' faces at the sides, and the 5:3 lake was blown up soft. The catalogue's "the user's photos used as they are" made the agent think otherwise. I would fit the two landscape photos first with crop fit: contain, lay a bouncy instrumental under the cut, and chain one comic caption per picture.

fix: Add a planner rule: "fun / playful / you pick the vibe" on a photo reel means music plus a playful treatment (comic captions timed to each photo, or short image-to-video moves), never bare slides. Correct the catalogue's assemble line: it crops every picture to fill the aspect and gives stills a slow push-in, so the user's photos are not "used as they are". Keeping a whole landscape photo needs crop fit: contain first; alternatively make assemble honour "fit: contain" in extra. The same gap affects every 'make it fun/punchy' reel and every mixed-aspect photo reel.
